lessons.title: Introduction to React
lessons.content:
# Introduction to React React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces, primarily for single-page applications. It's maintained by Meta (Facebook). ### Key Concepts - **Declarative**: React makes it painless to create interactive UIs. Design simple views for each state in your application. - **Component-Based**: Build encapsulated components that manage their own state, then compose them to make complex UIs. - **Learn Once, Write Anywhere**: You can develop new features in React without rewriting existing code. ### JSX (JavaScript XML) JSX allows us to write HTML elements in JavaScript and place them in the DOM without any `createElement()` or `appendChild()` methods. ```jsx const element =

Hello, world!

; ```

Hello, {props.name}

; } ``` ### Props (Properties) Props are used to pass data from a parent component to a child component. They are read-only. ```jsx ```

Handling Events
lessons.content:
# Handling Events

React events are named using camelCase, rather than lowercase.

```jsx
<button onClick={handleClick}>
  Activate Lasers
</button>
```

### Passing Arguments to Event Handlers
```jsx
<button onClick={(e) => deleteRow(id, e)}>Delete Row</button>
```

lessons.title: Conditional Rendering
lessons.content:
# Conditional Rendering In React, you can create distinct components that encapsulate the behavior you need. Then, you can render only some of them, depending on the state of your application. ### Ternary Operator ```jsx
{isLoggedIn ? : }
``` ### Logical && Operator ```jsx
{unreadMessages.length > 0 &&

You have {unreadMessages.length} unread messages.

}
```

React Router
lessons.content:
# React Router

React Router is the standard routing library for React. It allows you to build single-page applications with navigation.

### Basic Routing
```jsx
<BrowserRouter>
  <Routes>
    <Route path="/" element={<Home />} />
    <Route path="/about" element={<About />} />
  </Routes>
</BrowserRouter>
```
